clue.text: Taking it easy in Rome on vacation with pop star

indicators.note: a place on vacation has been emptied, so only the outside letters of Rome stay

parts.note: Sting is the British singer, formerly of The Police

explanation.surface: Someone lounging about in Rome on holiday alongside a famous singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' looks like part of the holiday scene but empties Rome to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at rest is relaxing, the synonym of taking it easy.

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a dish is an attractive person, someone lovely

explanation.surface: A painter alongside a beautiful vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovely' is the slang noun 'dish', a good-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-skinned peppery root eaten in salads is an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Work hard on a new catchphrase

parts.note: to slog is to toil, work hard

explanation.surface: Grinding away at a fresh catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto or memorable advertising line is a catchphrase, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Terrible derision about politician behind bars

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters wrap round the abbreviation for a politician
terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of derision are scrambled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A politician subjected to awful mockery ends up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges DERISION into IRISONED, which goes 'about' MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind bars is an idiom for being locked up in jail.

indicators.note: tucked into says the numeral for one is put inside the family word

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, a relation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into a relative's breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat, oats and other cereal crops are grain, a noun synonym.

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal

indicators.note: twice asks for the short form of Edward to be written two times over

parts.note: Ed is the usual short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A naughty Edward kept getting in the way, two times over.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to hinder progress, the same as blocking or getting in the way.

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters of Pinter are put to work in a fresh order

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea to read Harold Pinter's plays at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' looks like Pinter's dramas but rearranges PINTER into INTERP.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation is to make sense of it, a verb synonym.

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

explanation.surface: A weather report: the area has a typical temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or area of a country is a region, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Substantial sip of alcohol — a sign of nerves?

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Taking a good swig of whisky, perhaps as a sign of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substantial' seems to describe the sip, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic change is a large, striking one, so substantial is a fair synonym.

parts.note: kipper here is a sleeper, someone having a kip, and a sleeper's thinking is imagery while asleep, not a smoked fish

explanation.surface: Someone's mind is on smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, but here it is one who kips (sleeps), so a sleeper's thoughts are dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: The mental activity of a sleeping person is what happens in sleep visions, the joke sense of thinking.

clue.text: Tiny quantity of liquid around old sink

indicators.note: around tells us the small liquid amount wraps round the abbreviation for old

parts.note: a drop is a tiny amount of liquid

explanation.surface: A tiny drop of liquid sitting around an old kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like the kitchen fixture but is the verb, to sag or flop.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink downward or sag is to wilt, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Every other change hit back by European

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: back says the word for hit is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to tan is to beat or thrash, as in tanning someone's hide

explanation.surface: Every other change gets struck back by someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TAN (hit, as in tan someone's hide) to NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening on alternate days means occurring every second day, skipping one each time.

clue.text: Still writing stuff, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for writing materials is heard, not spelt, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: stationery is paper, pens and envelopes, the stuff used for writing

explanation.surface: A wry remark that some writing material is still around, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The two spellings are a classic trap: the -ERY word is paper and pens, the -ARY word means not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless is standing still, so still is a direct adjective synonym.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for line inside the river's name

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A neat line of boats kept under control on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A composed, self-possessed manner is a controlled one, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Train ophthalmologist, initially, to cut next to small pupils

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

indicators.note: to cut says that opening letter splits the following pieces

parts.note: by means beside, next to

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of ophthalmologist

explanation.surface: An eye doctor's training, with an operation on a small pupil of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' looks like the eye's, given the ophthalmologist, but it means students. O 'to cut' BY + S gives BOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys at school are pupils, so the definition is the general class they belong to.

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a ruction is a noisy quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: Prisoners argue tensely over a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is the quarrel (rhymes with cow), not a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure that has been built is an edifice, the noun sense of building.

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of deep cuts are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Felt material in which a gardener's spades have made deep cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' looks like the fabric but is the past tense of feel. 'developed' rearranges DEEP CUTS into USPECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sensed or had an inkling of something is to have felt it, a verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: taken over, as a town held by an invading army

explanation.surface: Seized while on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A seized country is held by the enemy, and a busy person is engaged, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Uncle is staggered about daughter's embraces

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for daughter
staggered means reeling, so the letters of Uncle is lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy uncle staggers around hugging his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggered' rearranges UNCLE IS into INCLUES, placed 'about' D.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace something as part of a whole is to take it in, a verb synonym.

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: new signals the letters of renovations made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Chat about some fresh home improvements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the renovations, but it is the signal to rearrange them; 'about' is the C of circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat or discussion between people is talk, a noun synonym.

indicators.note: after puts the word for anger following the hospital unit

parts.note: ENT is Ear, Nose and Throat, a hospital department
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury after a hospital ward is full to capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and complete, nothing missing, so full is an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Port in case served up by nurse

indicators.note: by means beside, so the word for nurse sits next to the reversed piece
served up in a down clue means the word goes upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: so can mean in order that, in case of need
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: A lawyer's case served up by a nurse at a port.
explanation.walkthrough: OSTEND is a Belgian ferry port.
explanation.definitionFit: This Belgian seaside town is a ferry port, an example of the category.

indicators.note: back says those concealed letters are read in reverse
holds says the letters sit inside the run of the words Pupil guiltily

explanation.surface: A schoolchild guiltily hides some fruit behind their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds ILGU across 'pupIL GUiltily'; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Jamaican citrus is a cross of grapefruit and tangerine, so it is an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Fliers from RAF please no Liberal, having taken off loudly

indicators.note: liberal means free, so the remaining letters are freely rearranged
having taken off says a letter is removed from the run of words before

parts.note: F is forte, the music direction for loudly

explanation.surface: A plea to the air force: no Liberal on board, and the planes have taken off noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' seems a political party but is the anagram signal; 'having taken off' removes F (forte, loudly) from RAF PLEASE NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft are things that fly, so they are fliers, an example of the category.

clue.text: First to observe a relative haven

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of observe

parts.note: sis is a sister, a relative

explanation.surface: The first to spot a family member's safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert, figuratively any place of refuge, is a haven.

indicators.note: neglecting says the abbreviation for education is left out

parts.note: scared means terrified

explanation.surface: Mark is a frightened student who skips school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the definition, a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish left by a healed wound is a mark on the skin.

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: transported means carried off elsewhere, so the letters of distance are moved around

explanation.surface: A display of current being carried over a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' reads as carrying the current along, but it signals the rearrangement of distance; I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out or signal is to show, a verb synonym in the third person.

parts.note: live coals are burning ones

explanation.surface: An old tree on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean tree bearing small oily fruit is an example of a tree.

indicators.note: about says the word for an action goes around the title for a gentleman

parts.note: a deed is something done, an act
sir is the polite address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a job done concerning a certain gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something longed for or wished for is wanted, a past participle synonym.

indicators.note: in places the American abbreviation and the quiet music mark inside the word for broadcast

parts.note: to send a signal out is to broadcast it
P is piano, the music direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An American softly cuts into a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something for a while is to interrupt it, a verb synonym.
